definitions.gloss: labor shortage, staff shortage, being short-handed
definitions.explanation: A condition where there are not enough workers or staff to meet demand. A widely discussed social issue in Japan due to the aging population and declining birthrate.

examples.japanese: {人手不足|ひとでぶそく}が{深刻|しんこく}だ。
{人手不足|ひとでぶそく}で{店|みせ}を{閉|し}めることになった。
examples.english: Due to a staff shortage, we had to close the shop.

examples.japanese: {介護|かいご}{業界|ぎょうかい}では{慢性的|まんせいてき}な{人手不足|ひとでぶそく}が{続|つづ}いている。
examples.english: A chronic labor shortage continues in the nursing care industry.

notes:
USAGE: A four-character compound consisting of {人手|ひとで} (manpower, workers) and {不足|ぶそく} (shortage, insufficiency). Very frequently appears in news and business contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人手不足|ひとでぶそく}を{解消|かいしょう}する (to resolve a labor shortage)
- {人手不足|ひとでぶそく}に{悩|なや}む (to struggle with a staff shortage)
- {慢性的|まんせいてき}な{人手不足|ひとでぶそく} (chronic labor shortage)
- {深刻|しんこく}な{人手不足|ひとでぶそく} (severe labor shortage)
